For years that was simply how React forms were written, and it still works. React's own announcement of version 19 opens its Actions section with hand-written pending and error state as the "before" example. It's explicit, every tutorial teaches it, and many developers assume the
prop is only for Server Functions in a framework. The half that's true: the UI does need a pending state and somewhere to put errors. What changed is who keeps them in sync.

content.text: Both bugs from the opening are gone. There's no

ends when the Transition does, so a timeout goes to the nearest Error Boundary instead of freezing the button. And the error message is just the latest returned state, so a successful retry replaces it. React also queues submissions and runs them one after another, each receiving the previous result, so a double click sends two invites in turn instead of racing them.

blocks.title: A returned error still resets the fields

content.text: React resets uncontrolled fields when the action finishes without throwing, and an action that returns a validation error hasn't thrown. Return only the message, and the user's input is wiped exactly when they need to fix it. That's why the right-hand version returns the email with the error and renders it as
. Keeping that field controlled also works, because only uncontrolled fields are reset.
